sentences.text: Cephalaspis is defined by a headshield with a largely tubercle-free upper surface, a tapered rostral part, a narrow dorsal median field, and lateral fields extending onto cornual horns.
The animal had a pineal plate fused into its headshield and a smooth, continuous outer layer on its body exoskeleton.
It possessed a pair of pectoral fins.
The type species C. lyelli was described in 1835 from Early Devonian Old Red Sandstone in Scotland.
The holotype specimen of C. lyelli was approximately 24.5 cm long in life.
Agassiz erected the genus Cephalaspis in 1835 as a wastebasket taxon containing four species.
Cephalaspis is thought to have been a bottom-feeder due to its mouth being situated directly beneath its head.
Cephalaspis likely stirred up sand and dust with its plow-like head to sift for worms, arthropods, and detritus in the mud.
Osteostracans, including Cephalaspis, likely possessed the ability to sense electrical fields.
C. lyelli, named after Sir Charles Lyell, is the type species of the genus Cephalaspis.
Cephalaspis is classified as a member of the Osteostraci, recognized as close relatives to jawed vertebrates.
A 2009 study determined that Cephalaspis sensu stricto is the sister taxon of cornuate osteostracans.
A 2026 study identified C. lyelli, C. fletti, and C. producta as valid members of the genus Cephalaspis.
Cephalaspis belongs to the parent group Cephalaspididae.
Cephalaspis lived during the Early Devonian period.
Cephalaspis lived from the Pridoli to the Emsian, between 422.7 and 393.47 million years ago.
